summary: Bleu helps astronauts look after their physical and mental well-being on long missions. Instead of filling out a daily wellness form, astronauts can talk to Bleu. The voice assistant asks follow-up questions based on what they share and their recent health readings, then turns the conversation into a structured check-in report for later review by a psychologist on Earth.  Between check-ins, Bleu tracks trends in heart rate, sleep duration, and radiation dose rate. The dashboard flags readings that need attention and reminds astronauts when a check-in is due. Using simulated mission data, our prototype shows how a crew could stay on top of their health even when communication with Earth is delayed.
details:
On a long mission, astronauts need to keep track of how they feel as well as what their sensors show. Project Team Pulsar built Bleu to make that easier. Instead of filling out a daily wellness form, an astronaut can talk to Bleu about how they slept, how they’re coping, or anything that feels off. Bleu uses their recent health readings and what they share to ask relevant follow-up questions. At the end of the conversation, the app turns the check-in into a structured report for a psychologist on Earth to review later.

Between check-ins, astronauts can see trends in heart rate, radiation dose rate, and sleep duration. The dashboard flags readings that need attention, provides reminders when a check-in is due, and lets astronauts select a body area to explore related observations. A text option is available when speaking is inconvenient. Role-based access keeps private check-ins separate from the physical and cabin data available to the flight surgeon.

We built the dashboard with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Recharts, and the backend with Python and FastAPI. The prototype uses simulated ASTRA mission telemetry. For the language model, we run Qwen3.5 9B with Q8_0 quantization locally through Ollama (ollama run qwen3.5:9b-q8_0). Local inference allows the language model to respond without a cloud LLM request, which fits the project’s focus on delayed communication with Earth. The prototype demonstrates the workflow with simulated readings and a simulated reply from Earth.
